features.description: Establish green baselines and audit all live builtin registration sets before editing.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline failures, if any, are distinguished from sprint regressions.
The audit records counts and set differences for all live registration sources.
No unrelated working-tree change is overwritten or absorbed into the sprint.

features.description: Build a canonical, deterministic inventory over registry, spec, and shared prelude metadata with fail-loud validation.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests prove deterministic byte-equivalent ordering across repeated builds.
Every lightweight registry key, every AllSpecs key, and each prelude descriptor occurs exactly once.
`show`/`toText` are pure and `println` is effect/IO; `intToFloat` and `floatToInt` are present.
Negative tests reject missing class, unknown capability, conflicting overlap, malformed stdlib target, and empty inventory.
A compiling mutation that removes one prelude descriptor or registry entry makes the named totality test fail.
Both evaluator paths retain focused behavior tests for the three prelude builtins.

features.description: Expose the inventory through deterministic JSON and table modes on the public iface command and update help.
acceptance_criteria: Built-binary tests prove iface --builtins --json includes the full sorted, versioned inventory.
`ailang iface --builtins` contains the same names and classifications as JSON.
Invalid flag and argument combinations fail non-zero with no partial stdout inventory.
Existing module `ailang iface [--compact] <module>` golden behavior remains byte-identical.
`ailang iface --help` and top-level help advertise both flags consistently.

features.description: Generate the builtin reference from the canonical inventory and prove the end-to-end classifier contract.
acceptance_criteria: Regeneration is byte-identical and a deliberate edit to the generated reference is detected.
No authored builtin list exists in the generator, CLI renderer, or docs source; names come from the inventory API.
The reference page is reachable under `docs/docs/reference/` and describes the JSON contract.
Consumer acceptance proves the three required classifications and hard failure on unknowns.
Formatting, focused and full tests, lint, boundaries, and docs drift checks pass.
